text:
Anna L.: quick check — I grabbed a tiny nsys snapshot and a short torch profiler run for a cold-start repro (batch=1, seq=512). seeing a weird KV cache miss burst at step ~12. can someone look at flamegraph and confirm if it's a prefetch gap or a model layout issue? s3 link: s3://redwood-perf/tmp/mini-traces/2475/trace_ns.tar.gz

Mike P.: on it. can you paste the command you used to capture torchprof? want to run locally to compare.

Anna L.: sure — command was:

```bash
NSYS_PROFILE=1 python -m torch.profiler --schedule wait=1,active=3 --profile_warmup 0 
  train.py --batch-size 1 --seq-len 512 --save-trace /tmp/trace.prof
```

also ran nsys with: `nsys profile -o /tmp/trace.nsys --trace=cuda,osrt -w true -- python serve_minibatch.py`

Julia: can you attach the tiny `inputs.json` you used? reproductions often differ by prompt tokenization.

Anna L.: uploaded input and a tiny capture README to the s3 path. perf-bot also posted metadata: `perf-bot: artifact size 12MB, captured kernels: 37, kv-misses: 18`

perf-bot: uploaded artifact to s3://redwood-perf/tmp/mini-traces/2475/trace_ns.tar.gz (12.3MB). redaction_flag: false.

Mike P.: quick glance — flamegraph shows a hotspot inside `kv_cache::lookup` around that step. but need the torchprof stack to tie kernel to op. do you have a torchprof `.json`?

Anna L.: yes, included `torchprof_trace.json` in the tarball. also a tiny console excerpt where I printed the first few KV entries: `KV[0].key=abcd..., hit=false` repeated 5x then `hit=true`.

Ryan: I'm free to pick this up. plan: 1) pull the artifacts, 2) run the same capture with `--log-kv` enabled, 3) run a 2-run bisect that toggles the prefetch config (prefetch=true/false) to see delta. who should I cc when I upload a redacted trace?

Anna L.: cc me and Mike. also note: this run used ROI warmup=0 to keep trace tiny — in prod we usually warm up 2 steps. might be related.

Julia: small suggestion — run with `--batch-warmup 2` and capture a short trace to see warmup behavior. Sometimes the perf regression only appears with zero warmup.

Mike P.: if Ryan runs the bisect, add a tiny harness script that toggles `CACHE_PREFETCH` env var and collects nsys + torchprof in a consistent folder naming scheme. that'll make artifact diffs easy.

Ryan: good call. I'll create `mini-bisect.sh` and push it to the perf-playground repo. ETA EOD.

Anna L.: thanks — also please scrub any debug tokens before upload. we have a 30MB upload limit on the perf bucket for non-prod artifacts; if it goes over, ping infra to get temp quota.

perf-bot: note: bucket usage for /tmp/mini-traces at 28.9MB used out of 30MB soft quota.

Mike P.: FYI — when you upload, include a short `howto.md` with steps to reproduce and the exact env vars. helps future bisects.

Ryan: yep. will do. taking ownership and will paste results here when I have the two traces and the diff flamegraphs.

Anna L.: appreciated! :thumbsup:

Julia: if you need a second pair of eyes on diffing the torchprof stacks, ping me. I can run the stack-compare script.

Ryan: starting now.

Anna L.: small follow-up: if prefetch=false reduces KV misses but increases latency, we should record both per-token latency and token cost. we may need a knobbed rollout instead of a permanent disable.

Mike P.: agreed. capture latency hist as part of the bisect outputs so we can make the trade-off decision.

Ryan: noted — adding `latency_hist.csv` to the artifact set.

Anna L.: perfect. thanks team.
